stops.note: 'shepherd', from pascere 'to feed'; Christian Latin also used it for a priest tending his flock
a surname from Old French pastour 'shepherd'; Louis Pasteur showed in 1864, working on the wines of Arbois, that gentle heating stopped spoilage
applied to milk from the 1880s; Chicago was the first US city to require milk pasteurisation, in 1908

current_meaning: to heat food or drink to kill harmful microbes
